probes.question: Which kind of shape do people tend to link with the nonsense word “bouba”?
True or false: 4-month-old infants showed the same sound–shape mapping biases as adults and toddlers.

image.alt: A smooth teal circle beside a sharp orange twelve-point star on a cream background.

body.question: Two nonsense words: “bouba” and “kiki”. Two shapes: one rounded, one jagged. Which word do people tend to pick for the jagged shape?
body.reveal: People tend to associate “hard” sounds like kiki with a spiky shape and “soft” sounds like bouba with a rounded shape. It has been robustly confirmed across a majority of cultures and languages in which it has been researched. Even 4-month-old infants have the same sound–shape mapping biases as adults and toddlers.
